question.text: A 46-year-old woman presents with difficulty initiating sleep, as well as frequent nighttime awakenings. She reports making multiple mistakes at her office job, has an inability to concentrate, and feels sleepy throughout the day. She is worried that her sleeping troubles will cause her to get fired. Which of the following would best treat this patient’s insomnia pharmacologically?

The primary goal of pharmacological treatment should be to improve sleep quality and daytime alertness. Benzodiazepines (A, B, C) are generally not recommended as first-line treatments for chronic insomnia due to their potential for dependence, tolerance, and side effects. Modafinil is a wakefulness-promoting agent that can be effective in treating excessive daytime sleepiness associated with insomnia. Therefore, Modafinil is the most appropriate choice.
